title: Keep .env out of the image
summary: COPY . . quietly put the password into the image. Find it, then use .dockerignore so it never gets in again.

tasks.title: `found.txt` holds the password you found inside the `leaky` image
tasks.hint: Anyone with the image can look at its files: `docker run --rm leaky cat /app/.env`. Copy the value after `DB_PASSWORD=` into `found.txt` and save.

tasks.title: `.dockerignore` tells Docker to leave `.env` out
tasks.hint: Make a new file called exactly `.dockerignore` (with the dot) next to the Dockerfile, with one line: `.env`

tasks.title: The image `greet-clean` is built and has no `.env` inside
tasks.hint: `docker build -t greet-clean .` after saving `.dockerignore`. Check it yourself: `docker run --rm greet-clean ls -a /app`.

tasks.title: `clean` runs `greet-clean` on `http://localhost:3402`, still Tanvi on pink
tasks.hint: The settings now come from outside: `docker run -d --name clean -p 3402:3000 --env-file .env greet-clean`.
